dod_intent_evidence: Own site (tech/spacecraft) states the fleet will 'host and transit payloads for applications across the commercial, science, and defense sectors' and sells 'renewed space superiority', and they are hiring a 'VP of Government Relations' (careers section) — defense motion is stated in their own language, though no award or contract record appears in the pack.
score_evidence: 'We've demonstrated successful operation of our high-thrust chemical and high-efficiency electric engine prototypes' → lab_language_intensity (prototype demo as the proof point)

~983 words of propulsion/spacecraft detail with zero mention of ITAR, export control, ATO/RMF, CMMC or ground-segment accreditation → deployment_awareness_absence (capped at 12, own-language < 1000 words)
'delta-V in whatever form an operator needs' is the single operator reference; no CONOPS, mission-ops, training or sustainment language → operator_absence (capped at 12)

Careers list is propulsion, structures, GNC, fluids, mechanical, power electronics, embedded, plus one Test/Automation Engineer and a VP of Government Relations; no mission-operations, export-compliance or security engineering roles → hiring_profile_skew
Roadmap '2026 First spaceflight' then '2027 Operational missions start in LEO/MEO/GEO' against an $8M raise dated 2024-11-12 and 17 employees → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: No export-control posture anywhere in a ~1,000-word technical site that also solicits international interest
blind_spots.operator_reality: H2/O2 chemical and electric thrusters are USML-controlled; a government customer cannot put controlled mission data on the company's systems, and the 'Fly With Us' inbound funnel invites foreign-person inquiries that a program office will treat as an export finding. Contract vehicles stall on the compliance package, not the engine.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Founders came out of SpaceX/Varda where an existing corporate export and security apparatus handled this invisibly; at 17 people nobody owns it and no compliance role is being hired.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: We design, analyze, test, and manufacture our engines in house in El Segundo, California.

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Autonomous RPO-ready' is sold as a spacecraft feature with no ground segment, comms, or accreditation story
blind_spots.operator_reality: RPO and GEO life-extension are Space Force / SDA mission sets flown from accredited government ground networks. Tasking, telemetry and imagery ride on IL5-and-above enclaves that require an ATO, STIGs and a POA&M; a commercial ops center that assumes open internet links cannot be connected, so the demo flies and the mission still cannot be tasked.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The team is optimizing the vehicle equation (delta-V, thrust, payload power) and treats the ground/network side as a later integration detail.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Acquisition advocacy is being hired after the roadmap was fixed, not designed into it
blind_spots.operator_reality: The 2026 flight demo has to convert into a funded 2027 mission. Without a champion above the program-office action officer and a named transition vehicle lined up 12-18 months ahead, the demo lands in the gap between a $8M seed raised in late 2024 and the money needed to fly operationally — months-to-field exceeding funded months, which is the failure mode that kills the company, not the technology.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company pivoted from terrestrial CO2-to-fuel (the 2024 raise headline) into space mobility; government strategy is catching up to the technical roadmap rather than leading it.

opener_hook: Your spacecraft page sells 'Autonomous RPO-ready' to the defense sector, but across the whole tech section there is no mention of export control or a ground-segment accreditation path — the two things that decide whether the 2026 Trinity demo becomes a 2027 funded mission.
what_they_do: Builds water-fueled multi-mode (chemical + electric) propulsion and ESPA-class spacecraft for high-delta-V maneuvering from LEO to cislunar.
